meta.analyst_notes: Ulixacaltamide is a selective T-type (Cav3.1/3.2) calcium channel blocker targeting the thalamocortical oscillatory circuit responsible for essential tremor. Unlike propranolol (beta-blocker, CNS side effects) and primidone (antiepileptic, sedation), ulixacaltamide is mechanistically precision-targeted and showed substantially cleaner tolerability in Phase 2. Phase 2b PRISM: -50.0% tremor improvement (TETRAS scale) vs. -28.1% placebo; p<0.001. Only 3% discontinuation due to adverse events vs. 15-20% for propranolol. Investment thesis: ET is a chronically undertreated market because existing options are intolerable for most patients. A differentiated, well-tolerated agent could not only capture the current treatment-seeking population but unlock the 75% of moderate-severe ET patients who have never been treated — a much larger TAM. Praxis has multiple CNS programs (PRAX-628 for epilepsy), making this a platform investment rather than a single-asset bet.

asset.name: ulixacaltamide (PRAX-944)
asset.mechanism_of_action: Selective blocker of Cav3.1 and Cav3.2 T-type voltage-gated calcium channels. These channels drive thalamocortical burst firing, which is the neural mechanism underlying pathological oscillations seen in essential tremor (8-12 Hz frequency). By selectively suppressing thalamic burst activity, ulixacaltamide dampens the oscillatory circuit without broad CNS depression (contrast: propranolol, primidone).

company.notes: Cash runway: ~325/40 ≈ 8 quarters. Tight for a two-program company. Praxis may need to raise capital before ESSENTIAL readout (H1 2026). trials.primary_endpoint: TETRAS-ADL subscale change from baseline at week 12 (superiority vs. placebo)
trials.notes: TETRAS (The Essential Tremor Rating Assessment Scale) is FDA-validated for ET. PRISM Phase 2b used same endpoint; ESSENTIAL is powered to reproduce the -22pp difference in TETRAS-ADL seen in Phase 2 (50% vs 28%). Placebo arm is well-defined. CNS Phase 3 has elevated failure risk despite good Phase 2; patient heterogeneity and placebo response variability are the primary concerns.

Strong unmet need case (no new ET approvals in >40 years); likely standard review. Precedent: FDA approved Ingrezza (valbenazine) for tardive dyskinesia on similar evidence package (Phase 2/3 combination; hyperkinetic movement disorder).

what_would_change_thesis: ESSENTIAL Phase 3 success (TETRAS-ADL superiority with clean safety profile) → NDA submission; partnership discussions likely immediately.
ESSENTIAL Phase 3 failure → thesis ends; Praxis restructures around PRAX-628 only; stock falls 60-80%.
PRAX-628 Phase 2 positive readout → platform re-rating; Praxis becomes multi-asset CNS company; reduces single-asset binary risk.
Partnership or licensing deal (large pharma CNS presence) → validates data and removes launch execution risk; upfront + milestone structure.
Payer pre-approval signals (PBM formulary framework before NDA) → accelerates launch ramp; re-rates on commercialization expectations.
Additional biomarker data: oscillation biomarker predicting ulixacaltamide response → could enable precision patient selection and improve responder rate.
